stemBlocks.value: The speeds, to the nearest km/h, of 90 vehicles passing a checkpoint are grouped as 0–19 (5), 20–39 (11), 40–59 (26), 60–79 (37), 80–99 (9), 100–119 (2). (a) For the class 20–39 state (i) the upper class limit, (ii) the class width, (iii) the speed at or below which 16 vehicles passed. (b) Complete the cumulative frequency column. (c) Draw the cumulative frequency curve using 2 cm to 20 km/h on the x-axis and 2 cm to 10 vehicles on the y-axis. (d)(i) Use the graph to estimate the speed at or below which 50% of the vehicles were driving.
Think first: Cumulative frequency is a running total, and each running total belongs at the upper class boundary of its class, not at the middle.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p212-q03 from workbook page 212.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read off the limits and width of the class 20–39.

contentBlocks.value: Upper class limit is the larger number written in the class; boundaries are 19.5 and 39.5, so width = 39.5 − 19.5
Result: Upper class limit 39; class width 20
5 + 11 = 16 vehicles fall in the classes 0–19 and 20–39, all with speeds up to the upper boundary 39.5
Result: 16 vehicles travelled at 39.5 km/h or less (i.e. no more than 39 km/h as recorded)

solutionSteps.instruction: Complete the cumulative frequency column by running totals.
Plot the cumulative frequencies against the upper class boundaries and join with a smooth curve.

contentBlocks.value: Result: A smooth S-shaped cumulative frequency curve

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the median from the curve at half the total frequency.

strategyBlocks.value: Add the frequencies in turn to complete the cumulative frequency column, plot each total against its upper class boundary, then read across from half the total frequency to estimate the median speed.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a)(i) 39  (ii) 20 km/h  (iii) 39.5 km/h (the upper class boundary of 20–39).  (b) Cumulative frequencies: 5, 16, 42, 79, 88, 90.  (c) Points (19.5, 5), (39.5, 16), (59.5, 42), (79.5, 79), (99.5, 88), (119.5, 90) joined by a smooth curve.  (d)(i) Reading across at a cumulative frequency of 45 gives a speed of about 61 km/h.

whyThisWorks.value: A cumulative frequency curve answers the question 'how many are at most this value?', so each running total must be plotted at the top edge of its class — the only speed by which all of those vehicles have certainly been counted. Reading back from half the total frequency then gives the middle value of the whole distribution, which is the median.
